claim_boundary: This artifact closes the exceptional-multiplier weighted average for every edge multiplicity only under the two strict regional conditions. It proves no full paired norm, endpoint, moment, density, or prime intervals.

multiplier_fiber_height_theorem.boundary: this closes only the exceptional-multiplier weighted average in the stated region; no full paired norm, endpoint, moment, density, or prime-interval theorem is proved
multiplier_fiber_height_theorem.cancellation_identity: for coprime A,B and coprime p,q, gcd(Ap,Bq)=gcd(A,q)gcd(B,p)
multiplier_fiber_height_theorem.closure_region: all edge multiplicities meet the exceptional-average diagonal budget when rho<1/6-mu/2 and tau-3rho>mu-1/30
multiplier_fiber_height_theorem.fiber_bound: if A/B has compact height H and both p/q and (A/B)(p/q) have compact height N, divisor-class summation gives at most N^2 H^{-1}X^epsilon possible primitive p/q
multiplier_fiber_height_theorem.height_descent: an edge class |E_d|~J therefore forces height(r_d) <<N^2 J^{-1}X^epsilon
multiplier_fiber_height_theorem.weighted_count: the exceptional count becomes B_exc<<X^epsilon(N^4/J^2+D N^6/(J^2 S^2)); after multiplying by J^2 the edge multiplicity cancels exactly

remaining_target.statement: control rho>=1/6-mu/2 by curvature across multiplier denominators or compile the surviving high-height ratio graph
